findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:0 lacks a test that drives `story_advance --phase=INIT_CHECK` on a clean INIT story through a SUCCEEDING bootstrap and asserts that phase becomes INIT_CHECK and the worktree is created on disk. The recorded evidence maps this intent to `assertDevStartRecoversStuckInitCheckStory`, which calls `dev_start` on a story already stuck at INIT_CHECK — it exercises the new recovery command, not the `story_advance` success path. The atomicity fix defers phase persistence until after bootstrap succeeds; the only `story_advance INIT_CHECK` path exercised is the FAILURE case (edge intent). A regression in the success-path sequencing (e.g. phase accidentally written twice, or worktree not recorded on the story index after advance) would not be caught.

cli-engine.ts:4100 phaseDetectionFailed path: guard pre-check skipped but dev_start still runs first. If story_get throws (phaseDetectionFailed=true) yet dev_start succeeds (worktree created on disk), and the subsequent story_advance (line 4138) then fails its gate, the worktree exists on disk while the story stays at INIT — a partial bootstrap that contradicts the atomicity guarantee. In practice story_get is extremely defensive (catches all errors internally and returns null/empty, lines 416-426 of story-query.ts) so it essentially never throws; the risk is theoretical but the invariant is not enforced in code. The phaseDetectionFailed branch should either (a) run the guard pre-check before dev_start like the normal path does, or (b) add a try/catch around story_advance that cleans up the worktree on failure.
